sections.h2: Boone County offices and where to pay
sections.html:
Two county offices matter here. The Assessor sets the value of each parcel. The Collector sends the bill and takes your payment, at Room 118 in the Boone County Government Center (southwest corner, Ninth and Ash, Columbia). Call (573) 886-4285 or come by between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM on weekdays.

Columbia is the seat, and the Missouri River forms the county's southern edge. School districts include Columbia 93, Southern Boone R-I, Centralia R-VI, Hallsville R-IV, Harrisburg R-VIII and Sturgeon R-V. Each district adds its own levy to the bill, so a parcel across a district line can carry a different rate.

The county counts 84,371 housing units for 2025 and an estimated 191,746 people. Owners occupy just 57.7 percent of homes, a result of the University of Missouri, Columbia College and Stephens College drawing renters. A seller may find a tenant in the house, an investor across the table or heirs who live far away.

  • Typical home value (2020-2024): $272,800
  • Median household income: $72,758
  • Median gross rent: $1,088 a month
  • New building permits in 2025: 787

Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value, and levies apply to that assessed amount.

sections.h2: When a Boone County bill must be paid
sections.html:
You owe the bill when you get it, and the hard stop is December 31. Statements go out through November. Nothing in the mail by December 10? Call the office, since a lost envelope doesn't wipe out the tax or the penalties.

Mailed checks count as on time if postmarked by December 31, per RSMo 139.100. Street mailboxes sometimes get stamped the next day, so send it several days early. In person, a drop box under the shelter at the Ninth Street entrance accepts payments until midnight on New Year's Eve.

Starting in January, late charges climb monthly until the account is clear. A parcel entered in the back tax book picks up an 18 percent charge on that year's delinquency under RSMo 140.100, or up to 2 percent a month if the owner redeems before the sale.

The cycle repeats every year. Miss an appeal window and you wait for next year's notices.

sections.h2: What to do if your assessment looks too high
sections.html:
Appeals climb three steps, one at a time.

  • Call the Assessor the day your notice arrives. A brief informal meeting explains how the value was built and clears up many disputes.
  • Not settled? Fill out the Board of Equalization appeal form and mail it to the County Clerk, postmarked no later than July's second Monday unless the board moves the date.
  • Carry the board's ruling to the Missouri State Tax Commission by September 30, or a month after the decision letter if that is later.

The right to that last step comes from RSMo 138.430. Paying under protest is another option: write "paid under protest" on a check for the full bill before year's end, then give the Collector a written statement of the market value you claim. Once the appeal window closes, your only recourse is next year's number.

Informal hearings run from late April to mid June, so use that stretch well. Gather what shows your home's condition as of January 1: photos of damage, repair estimates, and any recent sale or appraisal figures for similar houses nearby. Ask the Assessor staff to walk through the property record, because an error in square footage, age or finish level is the easiest thing to fix.

Write down the market value you think is fair. You'll need that number if you later file with the Board of Equalization or pay under protest. Bring your notice, since the value and parcel details printed on it are what staff will pull up.

A plan from the Collector covers real estate taxes and Neighborhood Improvement District assessments, though you have to pay the current bill before joining. Each month's amount comes from last year's base tax divided by the months remaining, so a plan that begins in March spreads the base across ten payments.

December's installment is adjusted to the real bill. The balance must be gone by December 31, or the plan can end and late fees start. Payment options are a coupon with cash, check or money order, bank debit on the 5th or 20th, or credit card on the 20th with 2.3 percent added.

If your lender folds tax money into the mortgage payment, the lender asks for the bill and pays it. When that request arrives before October 1, you receive an informational statement noting that the lien holder asked for it. A statement lacking that note belongs with your mortgage company right away.

You still carry the responsibility. Penalties begin after December 31 even if a servicer was supposed to pay, so after a servicer change or a loan payoff, confirm where the bill went. With no escrow, pay straight from the informational statement.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax after a sale closes?
sections.html:
Whoever buys the property inherits an unpaid balance, since the tax is a lien on the real estate. The buyer pays the full bill by December 31, the two sides typically prorate by months or days owned, and no tax money changes hands with the Collector at closing.

Closings after October 1 need extra care. The bill can still print in the seller's name and go to the old address until the buyer reports the sale to the Collector or Assessor. If a bill for a sold house reaches you, forward the buyer's name and mailing address to the Collector.

Before listing, phone (573) 886-4285 to learn whether an earlier year is open, and pass that balance to the title company. For a sale landing between October 1 and December 31, settle in the contract who pays the bill on arrival and who updates the mailing address. Keep your own copies of paid statements for the years you owned the home.

For back taxes, RSMo 140.150 allows paying delinquent tax, penalty and costs to the Collector at any point before the parcel is sold. A cash buyer faces the same lien rule, and a clean payoff speeds any closing.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Boone County property tax?
faqs.a: December 31. Payment received or postmarked by then avoids charges, which build monthly from January. Bills are mailed during November.

faqs.q: Where can I pay in person?
faqs.a: Go to Room 118 in Columbia's Government Center on weekdays. The Ninth Street entrance has a drop box that stays open until midnight on December 31.

faqs.q: Does the county auction tax certificates?
faqs.a: Yes. The annual sale takes place on the fourth Monday of August at 10:00 AM on the courthouse steps and covers real estate with unpaid taxes.

faqs.q: When is the Board of Equalization deadline?
faqs.a: The second Monday of July, unless the board extends it. After that, you wait for next year's notices.

faqs.q: Do I owe the tax if I never received a bill?
faqs.a: Yes. A bill that never came doesn't cancel the tax or the late fees. Call (573) 886-4285 if December 10 passes with nothing in the mailbox.
